transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 50m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Monroe (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Miguel Torres (Redwood Solutions), Mark Li (BrightCart CTO), Sarah Gomez (BrightCart ML), Tom O'Neil (BrightCart Infra), Jenna Park (BrightCart Product)

Auto-generated Summary: See summary field above.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Alex Monroe: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Alex from Redwood, i'll run through an Optimize walkthrough focusing on quant profiles, we wanted to show INT8 and FP8 profiles and the quality vs latency comparisons. Priya is gonna jump into the console and show the profiling.
[00:18] Mark Li: Thanks Alex. Quick ask up front: our main concerns are tail latency for the recommendation scoring and cost. We're running a couple of transformer models right now, complex attention stuff.
[00:30] Priya Shah: Great, thanks Mark. We'll show the Optimize suggestions, the predicted token latency and also the delta in quality measured by our eval harness. Note there are tradeoffs per sequence length.
[00:45] Sarah Gomez: Quick Q - how deterministic is FP8 vs INT8? We saw some drift when we tried quantization in-house last quarter.
[00:55] Priya Shah: yeah, great question. FP8 can preserve more dynamic range which helps for some layers; INT8 is more aggressive but cheaper. In our tests FP8 kept ~99.2% of accuracy for long-form completion on some models, while INT8 was more variable, but the runtime difference is often 20-40% faster for INT8 on some hardware.
[01:20] Miguel Torres: just to add, Redwood Optimize will generate quant profiles per model and per sequence length bucket; it also suggests fallback profiles for tail latency. We often recommend running both profiles in an A/B or canary for 48 hours to measure real traffic impact.
[01:40] Tom O'Neil: Are these numbers on NVIDIA H100 or A100? Our Dedicated infra is A100s.
[01:48] Priya Shah: Good callout. The sample numbers i show are mixed; we tested on H100 and A100. For A100 INT8 gains were a bit smaller compared to H100's FP8 kernels; FP8 benefit on H100 can be larger. We'll annotate the benchmark spreadsheet with hardware.
[02:10] Jenna Park: Also want to know if there are issues with output distribution changes - even small shifts can affect downstream ranking.
[02:18] Alex Monroe: Absolutely. That's why Optimize ties quality regressions to eval sets / prompt sets. We can run your scoring prompts and compute MRR / hit-rate / false positive changes.
[02:31] Mark Li: Walk me through a sample RB scenario - what's the expected latency improvement and cost delta?
[02:38] Priya Shah: Sure. For a mid-sized recommendation model (approx 1.3B weights), our internal numbers: INT8 reduced token cost by ~45% and 30% lower p50 latency; FP8 had ~30% cost reduction but better quality retention, p50 latency reduction ~20%. For long sequences numbers shift, and prefix caching affects results.
[03:05] Sarah Gomez: When you say quality retention, what metric? Perplexity? We use NDCG and business-specific conversion delta.
[03:12] Priya Shah: We measure multiple: perplexity for generative, NDCG/MRR for ranking; also task-specific evals. For BrightCart we'll map to your NDCG. We'll produce the delta table in the benchmark sheet.
[03:27] Miguel Torres: I'll share a link to the spreadsheet after the call - includes sequence buckets, hardware, and suggested profiles.
[03:35] Alex Monroe: ok i'm going to share screen, show Redwood Console -> Optimize -> Quant Profiles. Apologies if the auto captions are off.
[03:48] [screen share noise]
[04:05] Priya Shah: On the console you'll see 'Suggested Profiles' - we have per-layer calibration and two top picks: profile-int8-fast and profile-fp8-balanced. You can preview predicted metrics: token latency, throughput, and a quality score delta relative to baseline.
[04:30] Mark Li: That quality score is generated by Redwood's eval harness? Is that configurable?
[04:36] Priya Shah: Yes it's from our eval harness; you can plug in your eval sets. We'll run with your NDCG set. The score is configurable and we surface confidence intervals.
[04:50] Sarah Gomez: Any gotchas with KV cache when switching quant? We use a lot of caching in our real-time pipeline.
[04:57] Priya Shah: Great point - switching quant profiles may require warm KV cache and we recommend a ramp-up. Also some runtimes recompile kernels; we pre-warm in our Dedicated flows to minimize cold-start tail.
[05:20] Tom O'Neil: For Dedicated, is there any maintenance window impact when rolling quant profiles?
[05:26] Alex Monroe: We support canary rollouts and automatic fallback. You can push a profile to a subset of pods and monitor. If latency or quality drops exceed thresholds, Redwood can auto-fallback to a safer profile.
[05:40] [10s pause] Miguel Torres: i'm posting the link to the benchmark template in chat: https://redwood.example.com/sheets/quant-bench-template (internal link)
[05:50] Mark Li: nice. We'll fill in our request id's.
[06:00] Priya Shah: Now i'll show a quick side-by-side comparison - here's a chart from a recent retail customer. X-axis is sequence length, Y-axis is relative latency. INT8 is blue, FP8 is orange. You can see INT8 wins in short sequences, FP8 narrows the gap as sequence length grows and preserves quality better.
[06:23] Sarah Gomez: Do you log per-token latency? We need tail percentiles to 99.9.
[06:30] Priya Shah: Yes, Console exposes token-level latency distributions and cost breakdown. We can export per-token traces to S3 for deeper analysis.
[06:42] Mark Li: Can you show how to configure the Optimize rule that picks a profile based on region / model variant?
[06:50] Priya Shah: Sure - in Rules -> Routing you can set policy: prefer lowest-cost under p95 < Xms, or prefer highest-quality if conversion delta > Y. We demo a preset rule "latency-first" and "quality-first".
[07:08] Jenna Park: If quality-first executes FP8 in EU but INT8 in US, is there cross-region drift we need to worry about?
[07:16] Miguel Torres: That can happen. We recommend running spot-check evals in each region pre-rollout. The console can schedule periodic eval runs to detect drift.
[07:30] Sarah Gomez: About the eval harness, what format do you accept? JSONL, parquet?
[07:34] Priya Shah: JSONL or CSV with input/output pairs. We accept compressed archives. We'll provide a manifest template.
[07:45] Mark Li: Okay, walk me through the benchmark plan you recommended.
[07:49] Alex Monroe: The plan: provision dedicated test pool for 48 hours, run your 2000 prompts across baseline FP32, INT8 profile, FP8 profile. Collect NDCG/MRR and p50/p95/p99 latencies, token costs. We'll then produce a report and recommend a rollout strategy.
[08:10] Tom O'Neil: For the Dedicated test pool, will this incur extra cost? Need to plan budget.
[08:15] Alex Monroe: There is a short-term reservation fee for dedicated slots; i'll include estimated cost in the pricing doc. The savings projection often offsets the bench cost for medium-to-high throughput apps.
[08:28] [slight crosstalk]
[08:35] Sarah Gomez: We have some proprietary transforms in our model. Will Redwood Optimize be able to profile those layers?
[08:43] Priya Shah: As long as the model runs on our runtime and the graph is standard, Optimize's calibration pass will instrument per-layer stats; if you have custom ops we may need a short integration. We'll flag that in the spreadsheet.
[09:05] Mark Li: Security check - we need SOC2 docs, KMS integration notes for our key policies, and audit logs.
[09:13] Alex Monroe: We'll send the security pack after this call, includes SOC 2 sig pages, KMS/HSM overview for Private deployments, and examples of audit logs.
[09:25] Jenna Park: Also compliance for EU customers - data residency is a must.
[09:29] Miguel Torres: We support region pinned deployments and can run the tests in EU if needed.
[09:36] Priya Shah: Quick demo note: when you click "generate profile", Optimize runs a calibration step - it samples activations and suggests scaling factors. That process can take a few minutes depending on model size. We store the profile and you can label it.
[09:56] Sarah Gomez: If the calibration runs change weights slightly, can that break reproducibility for A/B tests?
[10:02] Priya Shah: Profiles are deterministic given the calibration seed we used; but small numeric differences can occur. We recommend storing baseline outputs and gating via canaries.
[10:18] Mark Li: Let's talk about rollout strategy - we prefer canary -> 10% -> 50% -> full with automatic rollback.
[10:25] Alex Monroe: That's our recommended approach, and Console has an automated rollout policy you can attach checks to.
[10:33] Miguel Torres: i'll add a suggested monitor set: p50/p95/p99 latency, NDCG delta, token cost delta, error rate.
[10:40] Tom O'Neil: Are there any failure modes specific to INT8 that we should test for?
[10:46] Priya Shah: INT8 can produce outliers if calibration doesn't capture extreme activations; we recommend stress tests with adversarial inputs. Also watch for layerwise saturation.
[10:58] [short pause as participants take notes]
[11:05] Alex Monroe: We're about halfway through, any other big topics?
[11:09] Mark Li: No, but want to confirm metrics we'll get back - can you break out cost by token and show projected savings for our 1M daily requests?
[11:18] Alex Monroe: Yep we'll include a cost model in the follow-up.
[11:22] Priya Shah: i'm going to walk through a live sample run - running baseline FP32, then INT8, then FP8 on the same input. You'll see slight differences in top-k and scores. Remember this is demo traffic so numbers will vary.
[11:38] [typing/screen noise]
[12:00] Priya Shah: FP32 baseline: NDCG 0.842. INT8: 0.828 (delta -0.014), FP8: 0.839 (delta -0.003). Latency p95: baseline 120ms, INT8 85ms, FP8 95ms. Token cost per 1k tokens: baseline $0.12, INT8 $0.066, FP8 $0.084.
[12:30] Sarah Gomez: Those deltas are helpful. Any way to tune INT8 to recover quality?
[12:36] Priya Shah: You can use mixed precision - e.g., keep sensitive layers in FP16/FP32 and quantize the rest. Optimize supports hybrid profiles. That often recovers most quality while keeping cost gains.
[12:52] Mark Li: For our scoring model, would you recommend mixed precision or FP8?
[12:58] Priya Shah: Based on what you've said (importance of conversion metrics), i'd recommend FP8-balanced as first pass, then run a targeted INT8 with hybrid layers if FP8 doesn't meet latency goals. The benchmark will validate.
[13:12] Miguel Torres: i'm noting that for long sequences (>1024 tokens) FP8 often edges ahead on quality retention.
[13:18] Tom O'Neil: about autoscaling - will quant profiles interact with autoscaler decisions?
[13:25] Alex Monroe: Yes, profiles change per-token compute. Autoscaler uses observed throughput and CPU/GPU metrics; if you switch to INT8 you may see higher throughput so autoscaler thresholds might need adjusting.
[13:40] Jenna Park: Any impact on model update process? When we push a new model, profiles need regen?
[13:45] Priya Shah: Right - profiles are model-version specific. We recommend regenerating profiles post model change. Console can automate that as part of CI pipelines.
[14:00] Mark Li: timeline question - we want this in prod in 6 weeks if results are good. Feasible?
[14:06] Alex Monroe: Yes, 6 weeks is reasonable: 1 week for data prep, 2-3 days bench, review & adjustments 1 week, canary rollouts the following. We'll map milestones in the follow-up.
[14:20] Sarah Gomez: Great. Anything else we should feed you for the bench?
[14:24] Alex Monroe: The sample prompts, current baseline outputs, and a representative traffic trace (anonymized) will help. Sarah said she'd provide prompts; Tom will give networking notes.
[14:35] Mark Li: ok. Last Q - if we see regression post-rollout, how fast can we rollback?
[14:41] Priya Shah: Rollback is immediate; canary rules can auto-fallback within seconds if thresholds exceeded. We'll also keep historical profiles for fast switches.
[14:53] Miguel Torres: posting the security pack link in chat now: https://redwood.example.com/security/pack (internal)
[15:00] Alex Monroe: Cool - i'll capture action items. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the bench template, pricing, and security docs.
[15:07] Mark Li: thanks all.
[15:10] [call ends]
